elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language expressly provides that Customer may terminate “for convenience at any time.”

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 90 days' notice, not 30 days' notice.

elements.element: Customer's termination notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The added termination right expressly requires “written notice.”

elements.element: Vendor must refund prepaid fees following Customer's termination for convenience.
The refund of prepaid fees must be calculated on a pro-rata basis.
elements.evidence: No pro-rata refund language is included.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The existing clause permits termination by “either Party” on 90 days' written notice and does not expressly limit Vendor's termination right to the end of a term.

elements.element: Customer has a right to terminate the Agreement for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The added language permits Customer, defined as the Company, to terminate “for convenience at any time.”

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires between 60 and 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The added language requires 90 days' written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed 3 months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is expressly capped at “not exceeding 3 months' fees.”

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Although the termination provision appears within an automatic-renewal clause, it allows either Party to terminate and requires the notice to specify a Termination Date; it does not expressly restrict Vendor's Termination Date to the end of a term.

elements.element: Vendor's end-of-term convenience termination requires 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The existing bilateral termination language requires ninety days' written notice from either Party, which includes Vendor.

result.reason: The redline adds the fallback Customer right on 90 days' written notice and caps the Termination Payment at three months' fees. It does not attain the preferred position because it lacks 30-day notice and a pro-rata prepaid-fee refund. It also fails the complete fallback because Vendor's existing termination right is not expressly limited to the end of a term. The edits are targeted and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms, but the Vendor timing remains ambiguous and “3 months' fees” may require a clearer defined calculation basis.
